text: Cashew nut drying and storage (ការហាល/សម្ងួត និងការរក្សាទុកគ្រាប់ស្វាយចន្ទី) begins immediately after separating the nut from the cashew apple. First remove obviously immature, moldy, insect-damaged, or broken nuts and foreign material (soil, leaves, stones). Dry raw nuts on a clean, dry surface protected from soil, animals, standing water, and sudden rain; sun-drying works well in the dry season (រដូវប្រាំង), spread so air circulates and turned periodically. In the wet season (រដូវវស្សា), drying is harder and a covered drying area or shared drying service becomes important -- the main risk is trying to store nuts before they're adequately dry just to clear the drying area before rain; never seal damp nuts in bags to protect them from rain instead of finishing drying properly. Allow nuts to cool in a clean, protected area before storage -- do not seal warm nuts, which traps condensation. Once dry, store in a dry, clean, pest-resistant place off the ground (pallets, raised platforms, or clean wooden supports reduce moisture transfer) and inspect regularly for mold, insects, dampness, unusual odors, and damaged bags. Cashew does not need cold-chain storage once properly dried as a raw nut -- this differs from fresh vegetables. Do not give one universal moisture percentage target; the commercial specification should be checked with the intended buyer or a current Cambodian technical source. M23 is a documented Cambodian cashew selection, but do not assume it's the dominant variety on a specific Preah Vihear farm without local evidence -- ask the farmer which variety they have, and if unknown, use general drying/storage guidance rather than guessing.
